items.title: When police charged an NRL star, one detective broke ranks
items.description: As the footballer, shirt torn, face bloodied and with a concussion, paced his police cell, a veteran detective's phone started to ring.

items.title: Former wife of tobacco baron alleges horrific life entangled in illegal trade
items.description: After an arranged marriage to tobacco baron Sam Albion, Kawther Salih says the relationship spiralled into an abusive situation that saw her subjugated into working in the underground tobacco industry.

items.title: Live: Minimum wage increase to affect millions of Australian workers
items.description: A decision on how much the minimum wage will increase will be announced this morning, affecting the pay packets of millions of Australians. Track the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: What the polls reveal about One Nation's growing appeal
items.description: The One Nation leader, whose popularity has soared in the past 12 months, would be the first to say she doesn't put too much stock in the numbers.

items.title: Live: Chalmers not concerned about first home buyers falling into negative equity
items.description: The treasurer says he's not concerned about first home buyers falling into negative equity if prices fall because property is a "longer-term" investment. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Gas workers strike as negotiations on pay deal stall
items.description: Australian workers at the Japanese gas company Inpex walked off the job this morning, and plan to strike again this evening.

items.title: How batteries muscled out gas and pushed power prices down
items.description: Fossil fuels, which have powered the global economy for centuries, are under threat. And Australia has become ground zero in this global battle.

items.title: Trump rejects Iranian reports of peace talk suspension
items.description: Iranian state media is reporting that the country's government has halted negotiations with the United States over an end to the war in the Middle East, in protest over Israel's conduct in Lebanon.

items.title: Neighbours complain about 200 chopper flights a week into luxury resort
items.description: A luxury resort that has been shut for three years hopes to reopen by chauffeuring guests down a steep 4WD track and flying them in on more than 200 helicopter flights a week.

items.title: Workmate of missing Jack McLennan says he's 'given police absolutely everything'
items.description: The last known person to see missing Queensland man Jack McLennan alive has broken his public silence amid intense community speculation over his role in Mr McLennan's disappearance.

items.title: NDAs to be waived for landmark military sexual violence inquiry
items.description: Gag orders imposed on former and current Defence personnel who experienced sexual violence will not be enforced, allowing them to participate in a landmark military sexual violence inquiry.

items.title: Tax deduction red flags on the ATO's radar
items.description: The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) is warning Australians to stop claiming private expenses on their tax returns. The agency gives its tips this tax time, including the dos and don'ts of claiming work-related expenses and investment losses.

items.title: UK's ex-US envoy slams 'bereft' Starmer leadership in new document drop
items.description: Among the more than 1,500 pages of documents were messages from Peter Mandelson voicing strong criticisms of Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's leadership of the UK government.

items.title: Race to develop Ebola vaccine as deadly strain of virus spreads
items.description: Nearly 250 people are suspected to have died, and more than 1,100 are infected with the rare strain of Ebola in the DRC and Uganda, though the true spread of the virus is feared to be much wider.

items.title: Quiz: Are you smart enough to understand the Scripps Spelling Bee?
items.description: We don't think you'll have even heard of most of these words, let alone know how to spell them.

items.title: Growing up in a cult partly inspired performer's latest show
items.description: Carly Sheppard is perhaps best known for experimental performance, but a coincidental meeting with a fellow dancer convinced her to go back to her roots.

items.title: Why make-up sex may not be fixing anything
items.description: Experts say if a fight keeps ending up in the bedroom, it could be a sign you and your partner aren't resolving anything.

items.title: Record number of Australian billionaires hold total wealth of $686b
items.description: Australia now has 178 billionaires who collectively hold more than $686 billion in wealth, sparking debate about the advantages and disadvantages of the growing number of ultra-wealthy.

items.title: The impact of Australia only buying second-hand submarines under AUKUS
items.description: Australia will only buy second-hand Virginia nuclear-powered submarines from the US during the AUKUS stopgap phase, with some analysts criticising the move and others believing it is a positive change of plan.

items.title: Antibiotic found in wild seafood 14 kilometres from salmon farm
items.description: Tasmania's Natural Resources and Environment Department has confirmed the antibiotic florfenicol was detected at a 'low level' in wild seafood 14 kilometres from where the drug was administered.

items.title: 'Excited to be back': Serena Williams announces return to pro-tennis at 44
items.description: The greatest women's champion of the Open Era is returning to tennis after almost four years away, accepting a wildcard into the doubles at the Queen's Club tournament next week.

items.title: French Open Sabalenka's for the taking as draw opens up for number one
items.description: A series of upsets across Roland Garros leaves world number one Aryna Sabalenka in the box seat to win the claycourt grand slam after beating Naomi Osaka.

items.title: Changes to Victorian IVF laws introduced after Monash IVF bungles
items.description: The government is introducing amendments to laws governing IVF clinics that will allow the state's health minister to personally intervene to cancel a provider's registration.

items.title: Real estate agency using fake AI salesperson to spam customers
items.description: "Daniel" is an AI real estate agent who calls strangers and secretly records conversations without their consent.

items.title: 'A fifth of the price': Council uses AI for 10-year strategic plan
items.description: A Tasmanian council says using AI for a strategic plan has saved them time and money, and will be used much more in the future, but a resident says the community consultation is 'completely lost with AI'.
